files.description: Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

Bike-share stations (48 rows, one per station): station_code (four-digit code with leading zeros, e.g. "0040"), station_name (text, a few with accented letters), district (same 6 districts as riders.csv; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), docks (whole number), opened_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD).

task_text: For every rider in riders.csv, find in stations.csv the station whose opened_on date is the latest one on or before the rider's joined_on date, and attach that station's docks to the rider. Keep exactly the riders' rows, one per rider; a rider with an empty joined_on, or with no station opened on or before that date, gets an empty docks value. `result` should be a table with the columns joined_on, birth_year and docks.
intended_computation: Read riders.csv and stations.csv; for each rider (file order kept or not) take the station with the latest opened_on <= joined_on (dates compared as dates) and attach its docks; riders with an empty joined_on or with no such station get a missing docks; columns joined_on, birth_year, docks; 400 rows.

acceptable_variants.notes: joined_on may be text or timestamps; birth_year and docks may be float with NaN or nullable integers; row order free; if several stations share that latest opened_on, the docks of any of them is accepted

intent_summary: Attach to every row of a first time-stamped table the value from a second time-stamped table whose time is the latest one at or before that row's time, keeping exactly the rows of the first table.
